subject: history
title: The Decolonisation Chain in Southeast Asia Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says Each colony won independence on its own, because what happened in a neighbouring territory made no difference to nationalist pressure at home. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - separate leaders and parties mean the territories cannot have influenced each other

The territories were linked by a chain: independence in one raised nationalist pressure in the next, because campaigners could point to a neighbour that had already won, colonial control weakened stage by stage, and the example was carried on - Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957, Singapore internal self-government 1959.
The chain ran the other way: Singapore won first and the example spread backwards to the Philippines
Pressure never rose; each colonial power simply chose a date at random

questions.misconception: Each colony won independence on its own, because what happened in a neighbouring territory made no difference to nationalist pressure at home.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: Each colony won independence on its own, because what happened in a neighbouring territory made no difference to nationalist pressure at home. Reteach point: The territories were linked by a chain: independence in one raised nationalist pressure in the next, because campaigners could point to a neighbour that had already won, colonial control weakened stage by stage, and the example was carried on - Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957, Singapore internal self-government 1959.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain what a transmission arrow does in the chain.
questions.answer: It carries the example of a territory that has just won independence into the next territory, where it raises nationalist pressure and weakens the claim that colonial control can hold.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the carried example and its effect: pressure up in the next territory, control down.
Scene 4 is careful with the words: 1959 brings internal self-government, the final stage of this chain.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state the last stage of the chain and what carried the chain to it.
questions.answer: Singapore won internal self-government in 1959, carried there by the examples of the Philippines (1946), Indonesia (recognised 1949) and Malaya (1957), which had raised nationalist pressure stage by stage.
questions.feedback: A strong answer gives the full chain in order - Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957 - and ends with Singapore internal self-government 1959.
